criteria.name: test_loss_finite
criteria.description: Test loss is finite and below 10.0
criteria.rationale: A non-finite or extreme loss means training diverged.

criteria.name: beats_uniform_baseline
criteria.description: Test perplexity is below the uniform-guess baseline
criteria.rationale: A model that cannot beat guessing uniformly over the vocabulary has learned nothing at all.

criteria.name: top5_accuracy_minimum
criteria.description: Top-5 next-token accuracy is at least 15%
criteria.rationale: The correct token must be in the model's top five at a usable rate for generation to function.

criteria.name: no_severe_val_test_gap
criteria.description: Test loss exceeds validation loss by less than 1.0
criteria.rationale: A large gap means the Stage 6 selection was fitted to validation noise, so the test result would not generalise.

criteria.name: generation_not_broken
criteria.description: At least one generated output passes every quality check
criteria.rationale: Weak generation is acceptable because the runtime falls back to retrieval, but a model producing nothing usable must not be promoted.

limitations: The training corpus is small for from-scratch language modelling, so absolute perplexity is not comparable to models trained on billions of tokens.
Generation fluency is limited; the runtime mitigates this with a quality gate and retrieval fallback.
The test split contains 203 records, so per-domain figures rest on small samples and carry wide uncertainty.
